newsitem.title: ITALY: Arias set to score in Rome's Olympic Stadium.
newsitem.headline: Arias set to score in Rome's Olympic Stadium.

text.p: Rome's Olympic Stadium, a site more used to soccer chants than operatic arias, will host the city's popular open-air summer opera season this year amid hopes it will soon be able to return to a more ancient setting.

Gianni Borgna, Rome's councillor for culture, told a news conference on Tuesday that the decision to stage Puccini's Turandot in the 85,000-capacity stadium, home to Serie A soccer clubs Roma and Lazio, was a great undertaking.

"To do this extrodinary opera in a stadium for so many people will be historic," Borgna said. "It is a challenge. The public might not respond but I think it's a challenge there to be won. We have to bring opera closer to the people."
A part of the giant stadium, venue for the 1990 World Cup soccer final, will be transformed into Imperial Beijing for the production of Puccini's masterpiece, Borgna said.
He added that moves were underway for Rome's Teatro dell'Opera to return to the 1,800-year-old Roman baths of Caracalla in time for millennium Jubilee celebrations in 2000.

The company had traditionally staged its summer season at the baths, a big tourist draw, until Italy's Culture Ministry barred it in 1993 for fear that musical vibrations and big crowds were destroying the ruins.
"About a million people are expected for the Jubilee and we can't deny Caracalla is one of the city's prime tourist sights," Borgna said.

He said the summer opera, held in Rome's Villa Borghese park for the past two years, may be back at the baths as soon as next year but would use an artificial stage rather than performing on the archaeological remains as in the past.
The baths will, however, open the summer season in July with a special concert to mark the 40th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of Rome, the founding act of today's European Union.
Carl Orff's Carmina Burana, also to be staged in the baths, will end the season in August.
"It is symbolic that this year the season opens and closes at Caracalla," Sergio Escobar, director of the company, said.
The Olympic Stadium was less well known to him. "I've never been to a match there in my life," Escobar said.
